inspection_scope: Complete supplied film plan reviewed as data: script, beat contracts, rhetorical chapter, setup boundaries, semantic centers, visual rules, dominant actions, before/after states, continuity declarations, environments, framing, and planned resets.

checks.evidence: Despite three declared setups, b1-b3 share the same central slab, small-left Bot, paper wall/floor, tile wall, pricing placards, receipts, and work-surface world while introducing three unrelated physical rules: target distance, receipt burden, and latch permission.

Receipt geometry remains specified outside the cost proposition: b1 and b3 both name the receipt pile as focal target, all three beats retain receipts in the depth planes, and every beat carries 'Receipt settling' into the next beat. The plan does not give those receipts a current meaning in s1 or s3.

In b1 the target/dart action competes with a declared receipt-pile focal target and pricing/receipt set cues. In b3 the latch/route action has the same conflict. These are unrelated semantic groups rather than repeated members of one meaningful group.

All three unrelated propositions use verbatim-identical staging: one central physical slab, small Bot at left, fixed wide camera, and paper wall/floor. The same environment and depth-plane list persist, and no continuity reason justifies the repeated composition.

The formal token lists are empty, yet receipts behave as persistent undeclared tokens through the shared depth planes, receipt-pile focal targets, and repeated receipt-settling overlaps. Their lifecycle, state changes, and destination are unspecified, and they obscure the target and permission propositions.

Pricing placards and receipts are planned in every beat, but no story, location, action, or balance function is established for them in the accuracy or permission setups. In those setups they are unrelated retained geometry.

The setup records promise hard cuts after s1 and s2, but the shot contracts preserve the same framing, Bot placement, central slab, environment, depth planes, pricing/receipt cues, and receipt-settling overlap. The semantic shifts therefore lack a substantive planned visual reset.

b1 identifies the target as hero and dart placement as dominant action but names the receipt pile as focal target. b3 likewise identifies the permission switch and released route as the action while retaining the receipt pile as focal target. The plan assigns incompatible primary attention regions.

The planned central actions independently encode the propositions: a dart moves to the closest circle, receipts accumulate on a tray, and depressing a latch releases a route. Captions are not required to supply those core action-result relationships.

setup_assessments.evidence: The accuracy setup is implicated in metaphor overload, obsolete receipt persistence, semantic-group competition, compositional stagnation, undeclared token persistence, purposeless pricing/receipt geometry, weak resetting, and a target-versus-receipt focal conflict.

Receipt accumulation meaningfully represents cost within s2, but the setup participates in the repeated central-slab composition and carries receipt settling into the unrelated permission setup, weakening the reset and extending an undeclared token lifecycle.

The permission setup retains the pricing/receipt world, receipt-pile focal target, and receipt-settling language despite a latch-and-route semantic rule, producing overload, clutter, stagnation, weak reset, and competing focus.

violations.observation: One repeated paper-workbench/slab world contains target selection, receipt burden, and permission-route machinery, with pricing and receipt cues present across all three rules.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Give each proposition a distinct miniature world or interface stage; retain only the hero required by that rule and hard-cut between the target, cost tray, and permission route.

violations.observation: Receipts are meaningful in s2 but are also focal/depth elements in s1 and s3, while receipt settling overlaps every transition without a stated semantic function.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Confine receipts and their settling lifecycle to s2; remove them from b1 and b3 and end their motion before the cut to the permission setup.

violations.observation: The target/dart and latch/route groups coexist with a separately declared receipt-pile focal group and pricing/receipt environment cues.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Make the target group the sole dominant group in s1 and the latch-route group the sole dominant group in s3; remove the receipt/pricing group from both.

violations.observation: Three unrelated propositions repeat the identical central slab, small-left Bot, fixed-wide camera, and paper wall/floor staging.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Recompose at least two setups around their relationship: frame s1 around spatial comparison, s2 around vertical burden/accumulation, and s3 around a route visibly blocked then released.

violations.observation: Receipts persist like continuity tokens although the declared token ledger is empty, and their identity, ordered use, changes, and destination are not recorded.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: End the receipt lifecycle inside s2 and remove cross-cut receipt overlap; if any receipt must cross a cut, declare its specific meaning, state change, and destination.

violations.observation: Pricing placards and receipts have no established action, location, balance, or narrative function in the accuracy and permission propositions.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Delete those cues from s1 and s3, leaving only location cues that support target comparison or gate-and-route operation.

violations.observation: Nominal hard cuts do not reset the planned set, framing, dominant silhouette, Bot placement, or residual receipt motion when the semantic rule changes.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Make each declared hard cut alter the dominant stage and silhouette, and terminate outgoing residual motion before introducing the next unrelated rule.

violations.observation: b1 and b3 declare receipt pile as focal target even though their heroes and dominant actions are respectively target/dart and latch/route.
violations.smallest_structural_correction: Change b1's focal target to the closest-circle contact and b3's focal target to the latch-to-route release; remove the receipt pile from both frames.

limits: This data-only review can assess planned structure and hierarchy but cannot establish rendered clarity, actual 360×640 glance performance, pixel visibility, motion execution, caption legibility, or listening/audio performance.
